gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Soundcore Liberty 4 NC ships without LDAC: Soundcore says the factory firmware does not include it and the app has to install it. Once LDAC is on, the earbuds leave multipoint, and Soundcore rates them at 5 h with ANC on (25 h with the case), not the 10 h that rivals quote.
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys 'best wireless earbuds under $100' (cited in every chat), Skimwire 'best budget noise-cancelling earbuds 2026' (cited) and SoundGuys 'Best LDAC headphones and earbuds' (cited twice). All three present the Liberty 4 NC as having LDAC plus multipoint plus about 10 h with ANC. None says LDAC needs a firmware update, and none gives the battery life in LDAC mode. SoundGuys' LDAC page does say in general that 'you cannot use LDAC with Bluetooth multipoint', and ChatGPT repeated that in two chats. So the multipoint part is partly covered. The firmware step and the 5 h LDAC battery figure are new.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's 'best ANC and battery' label for the Liberty 4 NC for the one buyer this question is about: someone who will actually use LDAC. In LDAC mode Soundcore's own rating is 5 h with ANC on, about half the roughly 10 h figure that ChatGPT and SoundGuys quote. That rating is below EarFun's 7.5 h claim for the Air Pro 4, but I couldn't find EarFun's LDAC-mode figure, so the two numbers aren't like for like. Our own row for the Liberty 4 NC is also wrong as it stands. It shows '9.85 h / 50 h' and '2 devices' with no LDAC caveat. It should read something like '2 devices (not with LDAC)' and add 'LDAC on: 5 h / 25 h rated'. It should also note that LDAC has to be added by a firmware update in the soundcore app, and that iPhones can't use LDAC.

findings.label: LDAC missing from factory firmware
findings.value: Factory firmware has no LDAC. You switch it on in the soundcore app (Settings > Sound Mode > Preferred Audio Quality), and that triggers a firmware update.
findings.source_title: How to Enable Liberty 4 NC LDAC Mode (soundcore support)
findings.note: Quoted: 'The factory firmware of your earbuds does not include LDAC support. Therefore, it is necessary to update the firmware.' The US product page has the same wording.

findings.label: LDAC turns off multipoint
findings.value: Multipoint switches off automatically when LDAC is on
findings.source_title: How to Enable Liberty 4 NC LDAC Mode (soundcore support)
findings.note: Quoted: 'Once LDAC is enabled, the earbuds will automatically exit the multipoint connection.' The product page's troubleshooting section also says: 'Make sure that you are not using LDAC and multipoint connection at the same time.'

findings.label: Rated battery with LDAC on
findings.value: 5 h earbuds / 25 h with case (ANC on); 6 h / 30 h (ANC off)
findings.source_title: soundcore Liberty 4 NC | True-Wireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds (soundcore US)
findings.note: Maker's rated figures. The page explains: 'In LDAC mode, high-speed transmission leads to increased power consumption.' Compare the maker's 10 h / 50 h headline claim and SoundGuys' 9.85 h measured, which our page shows (rivals don't state the codec used).

findings.label: Phone requirement for LDAC
findings.value: Android 8.0 or later with LDAC support; iOS not supported. On Samsung phones you may have to turn on the LDAC switch in Bluetooth settings, and Samsung pairing calls for earbud firmware V3.73 or later
findings.source_title: soundcore Liberty 4 NC | True-Wireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds (soundcore US)
findings.note: Quoted: 'LDAC is exclusively supported on Android phone systems 8.0 or above and is not compatible with iOS devices.' The page also says to use soundcore app V3.2.7 or later, and to turn off LE Audio for the earbuds in a Galaxy S23's Bluetooth settings for the most stable connection.

findings.label: Price, soundcore US
findings.source_title: soundcore Liberty 4 NC | True-Wireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds (soundcore US)
findings.note: The page shows $99.99 next to a '$20 OFF' badge without saying what that discount applies to. Best Buy and Micro Center showed $79.99 in the ChatGPT chats; I did not check those today.

findings.label: Codecs and dual connection, Nothing support
findings.value: Codecs: LDAC, AAC, SBC. Dual connection works over classic Bluetooth. The Nothing X app connects to only one device at a time.
findings.note: Taken from the FAQ articles 'What audio formats does CMF Buds 2 Plus support?' and 'How do I manage dual connection and connection priority on CMF earbuds?' The text I could read from these articles doesn't mention any limit when LDAC and dual connection are used together.

unsourced: EarFun Air Pro 4 and Air Pro 4+: I looked for EarFun's own statement on whether LDAC stays on with dual-device connection. myearfun.com and its community pages failed with a TLS certificate error, manuals.plus returned 403 and the Alza manual link redirected to an error page. Our page's 'not with LDAC' note for both is still not backed by a maker document.

EarFun Air Pro 4 / 4+: I looked for maker-rated battery life in LDAC mode, to compare with the Liberty 4 NC's 5 h, and for EarFun's list of phones that support aptX Lossless (Snapdragon Sound). I couldn't reach the maker site.
SoundPEATS Capsule3 Pro+: I looked for the maker's statement on LDAC with multipoint, the Android version it needs and its price. soundpeats.com returned HTTP 429 to both the fetch and storecheck.

CMF Buds 2 Plus: I looked for the US product page footnote that a search snippet said reads 'The LDAC transmission feature requires both Bluetooth connected devices to support the LDAC transmission protocol', and for today's US price. The us.nothing.tech URL returned 404 and checkout-us.nothing.tech returned 429. nothing.tech showed only a £49 UK price.
Nothing Ear (a) and CMF Buds Pro 2: I didn't reach the maker documents on how LDAC works with dual connection before hitting the tool budget.
